newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-SAB H1 seen hit by Edgars.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-SAB H1 seen hit by Edgars.

text.p: South African Breweries, the world's fourth largest brewer, will post a jump in half year profits on Wednesday, but the shine will be taken off the figures by poor results from retailer Edgars Stores, analysts said on Friday.
SAB, which also has interests in hotels, furniture and glass-making, has won market respect for its slick and rapidly expanding brewing operation.
But analysts said poor results from Edgars and Coca-Cola bottler ABI -- in which SAB has stakes -- would dampen its group profit growth.

"Edgars took people by surprise. They have to make that up from somehwere else. Brewing should be fairly solid and hotels will be okay, but they are coming off a strong base last time," said Tom de Trafford, analyst at Simpson McKie.
"Overall the results will be okay, but I don't think people are going to get very excited about them," another analyst said.
On November 5 Edgars posted results that showed attributable income fell five percent in the six months to end-September at 145.1 million rand.

A day later ABI said half year attributable earnings were up just one percent to 32.4 million rand and an extended capital base saw earnings per share dip two percent to 29.4 cents. The dividend was held at 11.5 cents a share.
Analysts were forecasting SAB earnings per share on a range of 167 to 182 cents, up from 162.5 cents last time. Last time's dividend of 57 cents was seen rising to 60-64 cents.
The consensus figures were for earnings per share of 176 cents and a dividend of 62.2 cents.

The firm's brewery operations are the jewel in SAB's crown and the business has been the focus of market attention recently after it announced in September a share offering which raised $413 million to fund its international expansion.

Analysts said the dilution from the new shares would be almost entirely offset by the fact that the funds raised are being kept abroad generating interest. The recent fall in the rand will also help the overseas funds wipe out the dilution.
"There will be practically no dilution," one analyst said.

SAB, which has a 97 percent share of its home market, has placed its international strategic focus on fast-growing emerging and developing drinks markets, entering early in order to gain a dominant position.
The firm has interests in central and eastern Europe, China and controlling stakes in breweries in Tanzania, Zambia and Mozambique.
The newly-raised funds will go to expanding these operations, but analysts said they expected little new information with the results.
"SAB keeps the market very well informed," one analyst said.
